findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q discloses a securities class action (filed 2026-04-06) and a derivative suit (filed 2026-06-22), both over the company's book-to-bill statements. That puts extra scrutiny on how the bookings and cancellation figures are presented on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The suits followed the -22.6% reaction to Q1 2026, and the stock rose 14.7% on Q2 despite them.

findings.finding: Growth is pass-through heavy. Reimbursed out-of-pocket expenses were $303.1M of Q2's $707.3M revenue (43%). Service revenue, revenue less reimbursed costs, was $404.2M, +10.5% y/y against $365.8M in Q2 2025, while reported revenue grew 17.2%. Year to date, reimbursed costs are $615.1M against $439.9M (+40%). A top-line beat made of pass-throughs is a lower-quality beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 grew revenue 26.5%, with reimbursed costs of $312.0M against $202.4M, and the stock fell 22.6%. That suggests headline revenue strength alone does not hold the stock up.

findings.finding: Spot is $665.96 at the 52-week high, +8.0% in 5 days and +7.9% in 20 days, about 59% above the company's own Q2 buyback average of $417.70 (it made no June purchases and has $527M left). 25-delta skew is +11.91 vol points toward puts, and short interest fell from 2.2M (Jul 15) to 1.6M (Sep 30).
